title.en: Carrier of Words: the Gramin Dak Sewak of the Thar
The postman who walks the sand

text.en: In a time of instant messages, a letter can still take a long walk through the desert. This feature about the postman Khetaram shows what it takes to carry words to faraway homes.

The piece opens with how a letter travels through the postal system to a postman and finally to a letter box.
In areas beyond the last railhead and where the road ends in soft sand, Gramin Dak Sewaks (GDS) are the only link between remote communities and their families.
Khetaram has been the sole postman of Somarad Branch Post Office in Rajasthan for fifteen years, in the Thar desert only 2.5 km short of the Indo-Pakistan border.
His left shoulder is slumped from carrying a mailbag. The regulation limit is 28 kg and the mail must reach the border within 24 hours of dispatch from Jodhpur.
He walks on hot sand where temperatures cross 50 degrees. Sometimes he delivers after sundown, and water is too precious to wash with, so he can only wipe his body.
Until 2001 he was known as a delivery agent. India has over three lakh GDS, who form more than half the postal workforce, serving places from Ladakh to Lakshadweep and the northeast.
After independence India Post aimed to bring everyone within the mailing range, growing from about 25,000 post offices in 1947 to over a lakh and a half today. Rural depositors trust the post office with their savings.
GDS selection needs another means of livelihood and only five working hours a day, which helps keep workers in remote outposts. For Khetaram, in a land of famine and one crop of bajra, the job gave a new lease of life.

problem.en: Why is the work of a GDS called invaluable?

text.en: They deliver where roads, trains and phones do not reach.
They carry mail and savings to remote people.
So they link villages with the nation.

prompt.en: What qualities does Khetaram's job need?

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking a postman's work is easy

points.en: Khetaram walks the Thar to deliver mail.
India Post serves the whole population.
